problem: The VLN field grew quickly after R2R (2018), producing many datasets, simulators, metrics and method families. There was no structured overview that organized benchmarks by how much the agent communicates with the oracle and what the task requires. Nor was there one that grouped methods by the challenge each one addresses.
motivation: VLN draws on NLP, CV, robotics and ML, so newcomers face fragmented terminology and results that are hard to compare. For example, prior-exploration and beam-search results get mixed with single-run results. The authors see four recurring challenges: multimodal understanding and alignment, sequential reasoning, data scarcity, and generalization to unseen environments. They argue these are a natural way to organize solutions and to point to open directions.
key_idea: Organize VLN benchmarks on two axes, Communication Complexity (Initial Instruction / Oracle Guidance / Dialogue) and Task Objective (Fine-grained Nav / Coarse-grained Nav / Nav + Object Interaction). Organize methods into four families: Representation Learning, Action Strategy Learning, Data-centric Learning and Prior Exploration.
insight: Several empty cells in the benchmark grid expose gaps: no fine-grained dialogue datasets and no oracle-guidance + object-interaction datasets as of early 2022. Most progress on R2R comes from VLN-specific pretraining (PREVALENT, Recurrent VLN-BERT, HAMT, Airbert), data augmentation (speaker-follower, EnvDrop, REM) and history/memory modeling. In the compiled R2R test-unseen leaderboard, single-run SR tops out around 0.65-0.67 and SPL around 0.60 (CMG-AAL, REM, HAMT, 3DSR). Beam search and prior exploration reach higher SR (e.g., Airbert beam search 0.78) but with very long TL or test-environment access, so the authors stress they are not directly comparable. The survey also points out that raw CNN visual features can hurt generalization, while high-level semantic features (objects, room/route structure) and object/direction tokens in the instruction matter more.
method: Benchmark taxonomy: 3x3 grid of Communication Complexity (initial instruction, oracle guidance via help signal, free-form dialogue) vs Task Objective (fine-grained route following, coarse-grained goal finding, navigation + object interaction). Covers R2R, R4R, RxR, XL-R2R, Landmark-RxR, VLN-CE, Touchdown, StreetLearn, StreetNav, Talk2Nav, LANI, RoomNav, EQA, REVERIE, SOON, IQA, CHAI, ALFRED, Just Ask, VNLA, HANNA, CEREALBAR, CVDN, RobotSlang, Talk the Walk, TEACh, MC Collab, DialFRED.
Evaluation review: goal-oriented metrics (SR, Goal Progress, PL, SPD, SPL, SED, ONE, OSR) and path-fidelity metrics (CLS = PC x LS, nDTW, SDTW).

Representation Learning family: unimodal/multimodal/VLN-specific pretraining (ViLBERT init, VLN-BERT, PREVALENT, Recurrent VLN-BERT, Airbert); intra/inter-modality semantic understanding; graph representations; memory-augmented models (HAMT); auxiliary losses (AuxRN, self-monitoring).

Action Strategy Learning family: RL with intrinsic/fidelity rewards (RCM, nDTW/CLS rewards, model-based RPA); exploration during navigation (student forcing, FAST backtracking, active exploration, Pathdreamer world model); navigation planning (waypoints, semantic maps, milestones); asking for help (rule-based or neural oracles).

Data-centric Learning family: trajectory-instruction augmentation (speaker-follower, filtering by alignment scorer or adversarial discriminator); environment augmentation (EnvDrop feature dropout, REM scene remixing, EnvEdit, counterfactuals); curriculum learning (BabyWalk, room-count curriculum); multitask learning (VLN + NDH, VLN + EQA); instruction interpretation (sub-instructions, multi-view instructions).

Prior Exploration family: self-supervised imitation learning, back-translation on test environments, environment-based pre-exploration, and pre-built topological maps. Flagged as not directly comparable to single-run methods.

Appendices: dataset/simulator tables (Matterport3D, Habitat, AI2-THOR, House3D, Gibson, LANI, Google Street View) and an R2R test-unseen leaderboard (single run / prior exploration / beam search) as of March 2022.

numbers_note: Survey paper with no own method or experiments. The appendix table 'Leaderboard of Room-to-Room benchmark as of March, 2022' compiles R2R test-unseen TL/NE/OSR/SR/SPL for other methods (Seq2Seq, Speaker-Follower, RCM, EnvDrop, PREVALENT, Recurrent VLN-BERT, HAMT, Airbert, 3DSR, etc.) under Single Run / Prior Exploration / Beam Search. Values are printed as fractions (e.g., HAMT SR 0.65, SPL 0.60). These are baselines from other papers, not this paper's results, so they are excluded. The SOAT row appears column-shifted (OSR 4.49, SR 58, SPL 53).
results: No experimental results of its own. It delivers a two-axis benchmark taxonomy, a four-family method taxonomy, and a compiled R2R test-unseen leaderboard. In that leaderboard the best single-run agents reach SR 0.65-0.67 and SPL 0.60 (CMG-AAL, REM, HAMT, 3DSR) versus human SR 0.86 / SPL 0.76. Beam search (Airbert SR 0.78, SPL 0.01) and prior exploration (Active Exploration SR 0.70, SPL 0.68) are reported separately as not comparable. Proposed future directions: external knowledge, the last-mile object-interaction problem, collaborative/multi-agent VLN, sim-to-real (continuous space, noisy localization, dynamic scenes), ethics & privacy, and multicultural/multilingual environments.
limitations: Coverage stops at early 2022, before LLM/VLM-based zero-shot VLN agents and later continuous-environment / ObjectNav-style methods; the authors describe the discussion as introductory and broad.

The compiled leaderboard mixes numbers from papers and the EvalAI board, has missing entries, and shows at least one misaligned row (SOAT), so exact values should be verified against the original papers.
The taxonomy lumps fine- and coarse-grained object-interaction tasks into one column and treats the method categories as non-exclusive, so category boundaries are loose.
